Stage 1: Digitization
•   Digitization converts speech(analog) into a machine-understandable format(digital)
•  Involves sampling followed by quantization.
   – Step 1: Sampling converts a continuous analog signal into discrete digital
       values by measuring the signal’s amplitude at regular time intervals.
          • Sampling rate (in Hertz) is the number of total samples taken per second
          during digitization. E.g., 16,000 Hz for microphone speech.
          • To accurately measure a sound wave, the sampling rate must be at least
          twice the frequency of the wave.
          • This maximum measurable frequency is known as
          the Nyquist frequency.
    ─  Step 2: Quantization - Once measured, these real-
        valued amplitudes are converted into discrete
        integers (typically 8-bit or 16-bit values).

conventions.heuristic: explicit nonnegative h for every node; admissibility/consistency are not inferred
conventions.optimality: minimum path cost requires admissible h with h(goal)=0; this engine permits reopening but does not certify admissibility
conventions.arithmetic: IEEE-754 double precision; priority ties and strict improvements use exact stored numeric comparisons

conventions.edgeCosts: edges count as one hop for selection; supplied costs are summed only for reporting
conventions.frontier: LIFO stack, reverse-push neighbors so the first ordered neighbor is expanded first
conventions.repeatedStates: mark discovered on insertion; ignore any later discovery
conventions.goalTest: when removed from the frontier, before expansion
conventions.arithmetic: IEEE-754 double precision; priority ties and strict improvements use exact stored numeric comparisons

conventions.update: Q(s,a) ← Q(s,a) + α[r + γ max over legal actions Q(s′,a′) − Q(s,a)]
conventions.timing: sequential, in supplied transition order; bootstrap from the table before this transition writes
conventions.terminal: terminal target is reward alone, even if a terminal-state row exists
conventions.legalActions: transition.nextActions, otherwise keys explicitly supplied in initialQ for nextState
conventions.policy: transitions are supplied observations; no exploration policy or greedy action is inferred
